title: UNIQUE Constraint
description: Learn how to use the UNIQUE constraint to ensure uniqueness of data in a column or group of columns.

data.text: The UNIQUE constraint ensures that the data in a column or group of columns is unique among all rows in a table. Unlike PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE allows NULL values (but only one NULL per column).

data.title: UNIQUE Column Constraint
data.content: Ensures email values are unique across all rows.

data.title: UNIQUE Table Constraint
data.content: Defines UNIQUE as a separate table constraint.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE hr.persons(
    person_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255),
    UNIQUE(email)
);

data.text: Behind the scenes, SQL Server automatically creates a UNIQUE index to enforce the uniqueness. If you attempt to insert a duplicate row, SQL Server rejects it.
Assigning a specific name makes error messages clearer and the constraint easier to manage:

data.title: Named UNIQUE Constraint
data.content: Creates a table with a named UNIQUE constraint on email.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE hr.persons (
    person_id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255),
    CONSTRAINT unique_email UNIQUE(email)
);

data.text: Both UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY enforce uniqueness, but UNIQUE is preferred when the column is not the primary key. UNIQUE allows NULL (one NULL per column), while PRIMARY KEY does not.
UNIQUE for a Group of Columns

data.title: Composite UNIQUE Constraint
data.content: Ensures the combination of person_id and skill_id is unique.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE hr.person_skills (
    id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    person_id int,
    skill_id int,
    updated_at DATETIME,
    UNIQUE (person_id, skill_id)
);

data.title: Add UNIQUE Constraint
data.content: Adds a UNIQUE constraint to an existing column.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE hr.persons
ADD CONSTRAINT unique_email UNIQUE(email);

data.title: Drop UNIQUE Constraint
data.code:
ALTER TABLE hr.persons
DROP CONSTRAINT unique_email;

data.title: UNIQUE Constraint Key Points
points: UNIQUE ensures all values in a column or group of columns are unique.
UNIQUE allows NULL values (one NULL per column).
PRIMARY KEY implies UNIQUE but does not allow NULL.
SQL Server creates a UNIQUE index automatically to enforce the constraint.
Named constraints are easier to manage and reference.
You can add or remove UNIQUE constraints using ALTER TABLE.
